verdict.line: You lose when you finish a trade standing inside his 175-range Feast after eating Rupture; you win every clean skirmish where you dash in before he can land it.

brief.thesis: Cho'Gath has exactly one way to beat you: land Q (Rupture) at 950 range to knock you up and slow you, then walk into R (Feast)'s 175 range for a true-damage execute. Everything else in his kit is a short-range poke tool you can simply dash past. The 55.9% win rate over 93 games reflects that you dictate most exchanges, but the solo-kill edge belongs to him because one landed Rupture into Feast can delete you from a trade you were otherwise winning.

theirWindow.when: Right after Rupture's knockup lands on you
theirWindow.what: He can walk into his 175-range R (Feast) for true damage while you're slowed and airborne. Disengage with E (Valor) immediately instead of trying to finish your own combo.

yourWindow.when: Both his Q and W are on cooldown
yourWindow.what: With Rupture (9s) and Feral Scream (13s) down, he has no slow, no silence, and no way to peel. Dash in with Q (Broken Wings), stun with W (Ki Burst), and unload autos while Runic Blade charges are up.

start.why: The 94.3% pick rate reflects the standard answer to Cho's Vorpal Spikes poke — extra sustain and AD keep your Runic Blade-charged autos winning early short trades.

boots.why: Lower cooldowns compound with your kit's already-shrinking Q/W/E timers, letting you reset Ki Burst-stun combos faster than Cho can re-cast Rupture.

core.why: Cooldown reduction on R (Blade of the Exile) lets you threaten Wind Slash burst far more often than Cho's 60s Feast timer.
Sustain and damage against his tanky HP pool, which only grows if he's allowed to stack Feast kills.
Lets you tank a landed Rupture-into-Feast combo and walk away instead of dying to it outright.

situational.when: if cho gath is stacking max HP off feast kills and you need armor shred to keep killing him
if the enemy team's magic damage (including feral scream) is adding up to threaten your all-ins
if you want more raw burst to force a kill before he hits level 6 and feast comes online

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacking adaptive force through sustained skirmishing out-damages Cho's passive Vorpal Spikes chip and rewards you for staying in extended trades rather than poking.

summoners.why: Ignite denies the healing from his Carnivore passive after a kill and secures the trade outright once your Ki Burst stun lands, which is how 95.9% of Rivens play this matchup.

playing.title: Dash through Rupture's cast
playing.detail: Rupture is ground-targeted with a visible cast at 950 range — use Q (Broken Wings) or E (Valor) to close the last bit of distance after he commits so you aren't standing in the knockup zone when it resolves.

playing.title: Block Feral Scream with Valor
playing.detail: Time E (Valor)'s damage-block window to eat the Feral Scream cone instead of the silence landing clean, since a silence mid-combo cuts off your follow-up entirely.

playing.title: All-in right after his Feast misses or lands on a minion
playing.detail: R (Feast) has a 60s cooldown — the moment he burns it on a wave or whiffs it on you, he has zero execute threat for a full minute. That's your green light to commit.

playing.title: Never finish a trade inside his Feast range after Rupture hits
playing.detail: Once Rupture's slow and knockup land on you, Cho only needs to close 175 range to true-damage execute with Feast — disengage with E instead of trying to land your last hit.

playing.title: Pop Blade of the Exile right after your Ki Burst stun
playing.detail: R's cooldown drops to 10s at rank 5 — use the stun window from W (Ki Burst) to land Wind Slash and the bonus AD before his Carnivore passive can heal him back off a kill.

playing.title: Don't facetank his autos
playing.detail: Vorpal Spikes adds bonus damage to every auto he lands in melee range on a near-zero cooldown — dash out with E (Valor) between combo windows instead of standing in extended auto trades.

playing.title: Deny him cheap kills near your lane
playing.detail: Feast only grows his max HP (up to 6 stacks) when it kills something, so contest low-health minions and jungle camps near top to keep his stat-check weak into the mid game.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, rune pages, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning — why each trade pattern and timing window works — is this brief's own analysis.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of Cho’Gath’s (Q) skill. Use Riven’s [Q] and [E] to dodge enemy abilities while closing in on their position.
